title: Design a cognitive support around an observed task difficulty

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A cognitive support should address an observed task mismatch and be evaluated through the person’s use. More prompts are not automatically more support; a diagnosis need not be inferred or disclosed.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Use1 fictional plan: time Tuesday 16:00; question “which room?”; change route omitted because the long instruction was lost midway. Use2 with three labeled entries: Thursday 15:00; question “is paper supplied?”; changes by the already agreed text channel. All three entries are present, but a new repeating alert interrupts the person four times and they ask for it to stop. No diagnosis or controlled comparison is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare completeness and burden, identify which support to retain provisionally and which to stop with the person’s agreement. Keep the distinct plan facts rather than declaring one universal solution.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person completes all steps using a chosen reader but the helper supplies one substantive answer. What support must the record distinguish?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The labeled entries support a complete second plan; repeating alerts add an unwanted cost. Stop the unwanted alert and retain or revise labels according to preference. Partial: count only completed fields. Incorrect: infer a diagnosis or force more alerts to improve compliance. Different occasions prevent a clean causal claim.
criteria: Support responds to a concrete mismatch
Benefit and new burden are recorded separately
Access and content assistance are distinguished

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Access reading and a content hint are different. Preserve both the completed task and the supplied answer; do not describe wholly independent content performance or treat ordinary reading support as failure.
